payload.text: We are taking over maintenance of the interface that moves laboratory results from the lab analysers into the ward record system. Nobody who built it is still here. The immediate job is to make sure critical results, the ones that need a clinician to act within the hour, reliably reach somebody. We are not changing the analysers and we are not changing the ward record system's user interface. We own the interface service in between and nothing else. Before we change anything I need to know what it actually does today.

object.statement: Section 4.2 of the interface specification states that a result flagged critical is sent to the on-call clinician's pager, and that if no acknowledgement is received within ten minutes the result is escalated to the ward charge nurse.

The routing module sends critical-flagged results to the ward charge nurse's worklist queue only. There is no pager transport anywhere in the codebase and no acknowledgement timer; the ten-minute escalation described in the specification has no implementation.
The interface test suite asserts only that a critical result produces a worklist entry. No test covers acknowledgement, escalation, or delivery failure.

Production logs for August 2026 show the service processed 214,880 results, of which 1,942 were flagged critical. The logs record enqueue events and contain no field indicating whether a clinician opened or acted on a critical entry.
A charge nurse on Ward 6 says that in practice the laboratory telephones the ward for anything urgent, and that staff treat the worklist as a record rather than as an alert.

payload.text: One thing that is already decided and I am not reopening it: the analyser vendor's flag is authoritative for what counts as a critical result. We do not re-derive criticality from the numeric value. That was agreed with the laboratory director in writing.
